title: How Money Approved for Return on a Car Rental Is Settled
content:
An approved refund settles to the original form of payment and in no other form, because a car rental
carries no credit of its own. This is the settlement basis for the Car Rental Rate Classes.

## When a payout line may be raised

A payout line is raised only while the rental record stands at cancelled, no show or returned. A rental
standing at merely booked, confirmed, picked up or closed carries no payout.

## How long settlement takes

The settlement takes the rate class's processing time, counted in business days from the day the refund was
approved, excluding weekends and public holidays in the renter's country of residence. The count is of
business days and not of calendar days, and the country whose holidays are excluded is the renter's own.

## Clauses no longer in force

*Each payout is raised against the original ledger line it reverses, so a rental with several lines settles
as several payouts and never as one lump sum.* That clause is **no longer in force**.

*A payout may never exceed the amount that original line actually collected* is likewise **no longer in
force**; the ceiling that now governs rests on the current basis.

The remainder of that sentence stands: the sum of a rental's payouts may never exceed its ledger total.

## Where the supplier declines

Where the supplier declines the refund the rental is closed with no payout and the renter is told which
supplier reference declined it.
